summary: Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Leigh earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010), having studied under Ha-u Kim and traditional teacher Cheonghwa.
Hoseong Kim is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Kim founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo (attested 2011) and served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).
Hoshu Mitsuhara (1928–2008) worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004).

Hotetsu Matsumoto works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Matsumoto held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and serves as a professor and Director of the Clinical Esoteric Buddhism Center at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Howard Resnick is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held an affiliation with Harvard University (attested 1996) and served as an adjunct professor at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 1997).

Hoyo Watanabe (1933–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961). At Rissho, he served as a professor (~1974–2004), Dean of Buddhist Studies (~1983–1989), and special honorary professor (~2004–2021).
Hozen Seki (1903–1991) was a figure in Buddhist studies who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian (1876–1953) studied at Paris and Strasbourg, training under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet. Specializing in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he held posts at Aramiyan School (1893), Sanasarian College (1894), and Yerevan State University (1923).

Hrishikesh Terdalkar works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics, earning a PhD from IIT Kanpur. Posts include IIT Kanpur (2024), Claude Bernard University Lyon 1 (2024–2025), BITS Pilani (2025–2026), and IIIT Hyderabad (2026).

Hsiang-Kuang Chou worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies and studied under Swami Shivananda. Chou held posts at the University of Allahabad, University of Delhi, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (all attested 1960).

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD from Temple University. Hu served as an associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. After training under Yinshun, Zhikai, Ruoshun, and Zhikang, he founded Fo Guang Shan, the University of the West, and BLIA, and served as abbot of Fo Guang Shan (~1967–1985).
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. In 1953, he founded the Buddhist Association of China and served as its honorary president.
Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (both attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Chang Zhi and Hsu Yun. He founded the Buddhist Text Translation Society, Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, and City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, serving as abbot of the latter (~1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1978) and Ohio University.

Hu Shih (1891–1962), a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Columbia under John Dewey. He served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Tan studied under doctoral supervisor Medawachchiye Dhammajothi, pursuing a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) studied under Huanxian Yuan. Specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, he held professorships at Chinese Culture University (~1963–1985), National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University (~1970–1980), and founded Taihu Great Learning Center (2006).
